So he was hero, but in <c.481>Vietnam</c> nobody know about that. So he was hired by <c.482>Mr. Highland</c> to run the dairy farm and <c.483>Bến Cát</c> here, actually to recruit–
00:59:45.239 --> 00:59:46.679 <v Edward Miller> What was his name?
00:59:46.679 --> 00:59:49.259 <v PXA> I forget his name, it was <c.484>Carter</c> something–
00:59:49.259 --> 00:59:50.038 <v Edward Miller> <c.485>Carter</c>.
00:59:50.038 --> 00:59:57.449 <v PXA> But it easy, you can find it in any book about the dairy farm in <c.486>Bến Cát</c>, run by <c.487>Mr. Highland</c>.
00:59:57.449 --> 00:59:59.079 <v Edward Miller> <c.488>Highland</c>.
00:59:59.079 --> 01:00:20.986 <v PXA> Highland, Australian businessman here. He run the business of the feather, of the duck feather, of the dairy farm. And he captured by the Communists, and then it was <c.489>Bob Chaplain</c> who negotiated with the Australian <c.490>Burchett</c> to release—
01:00:20.986 --> 01:00:22.289 <v Edward Miller> <c.491>Burchett</c>, oh, <c.492>Wilfred Burchett</c>.
01:00:22.289 --> 01:01:14.363 <v PXA> You know <c.493>Burchett</c>. Yes, he’s a Communist, pro-Communist. He would like to have the visa to go to <c.494><c.495>U.S.</c></c> but the U.S. refuse to give it to him, to see someone et cetera. And <c.496><c.497>Bob Shaplen</c></c> you know, Bob Shaplen, he’s a good friend of mine, he is working for <c.498>the New Yorker</c>. So he said, "Alright, I’ll make arrangements. You can order the Vietnamese to release Mr. Highland”—he was captured during the <c.499><c.500>Tet Offensive</c></c>—“and then I wi<c.502>ll tell Amer</c>ican Embassy to give you the visa to the <c.501>U.S.</c>” So the deal was made, so that’s why he was released anyway. So when the Communists, they need something, they capture the guy. Kidnap <c.503><c.504>Bến Cát</c></c>, they kidnap the guy, in Bến Cát. It was in November, I think. November '61.
01:01:14.363 --> 01:01:15.389 <c.505>November '61</c>.
01:01:15.389 --> 01:01:27.590 <v PXA> He was kidnapped. There were Vietnamese working for him. After that, Vietnamese worked for <c.506>Mr. Douglas</c> and then for <c.507>Neil Sheehan</c> at <c.508>UPI</c>.
01:01:27.590 --> 01:01:28.670 <v Edward Miller> What was his name?
01:01:28.670 --> 01:01:32.030 <v PXA> <c.509>Rao</c>, <c.510>Nguyễn Ngọc Rao</c>. He was translator.
01:01:32.030 --> 01:01:33.190 <v Edward Miller> <c.511>Nguyễn Ngọc Rao</c>?
01:01:33.190 --> 01:02:48.230 <v PXA> <c.512>Nguyễn Ngọc Rao</c>, R-A-O. The North Vietnamese, they don’t know how to pronounce their R’s well, so actually, he should be written in Vietnamese, “Nguyễn Ngọc Giáo.” But the North Vietnamese...Rao Reo Rao, you know, so they put “Rao.” And that colonel was never revealed until he was captured. And then he was captured, and then I was busy to cover the flood, the <c.513><c.514>Mekong Delta</c></c> <c.515>Châu Đốc</c>, because most current-run advi<c.516>sors [mumbles] in</c>vited to go to have a look at the flood. And then, so we stay at the province chief, Colonel Minh, lieutenant colonel...at that time he was major chief of province. <c.517>Nguyễn Văn Minh</c>. After that, he became two star general, major general, commander of Saigon command and then <c.518>the Third Corps</c>, too. And then, all of <c.519>Michigan State University</c> went there, and then <c.520>Walt Rostow</c> and then <c.521>Maxwell B. Taylor</c> went there, too. This is combat troops.
01:02:48.230 --> 01:02:50.057 <v Edward Miller> <c.522>November 1961</c>. Okay.
01:02:50.057 --> 01:03:28.219 <v PXA> <c.523>November ‘61</c>. So over there we listen, we had a cable, telling us to follow very closely the writer, the capture of the guy in <c.524>Bến Cát</c>, the Egyptian, and they gave the biography he was full Colonel Air Force. They keep it secret so the Communists did not know that. They capture him because they need stationary, typewriter, and all kinds of thing, et cetera. So they ask him to tell his people to buy that in <c.525>Hong Kong</c> for them. So after, they supply this kind of thing, he was released.
01:03:28.219 --> 01:03:30.219 <v Edward Miller> He was released for stationary?
01:03:30.219 --> 01:04:37.739 <v PXA> For stationary, including the typewriter and the paper. He kidnapped by the guerilla in <c.526>Bến Cát</c>. But the purpose of that one is very important. He was near D-zone. You know, there two important zone in the South, they call it D-zone and then the other one is, close one is <c.527>Tây Ninh</c>, another military zone. So they set up this one here, so you recruit the worker to get intelligence, work at the dairy farm. You see the point there? Another zone. Military zone. So they set up this one here. So you recruit the worker to get intelligence, you know, work on the dairy farm. You see the point there, you set up a dairy farm in <c.528>Bến Cát</c>? Yeah, near the communist military zone. So recruit local people to get that. At the same time, you train them to select the one, the good one, to train them in intelligence. To get information for the government and then for the American and Australian here. You see the point? But they didn't know about that. They kidnapped him just for stationery.
01:04:37.739 --> 01:04:41.539 <v Edward Miller> I see, so the Americans were using the dairy farm to get intelligence?
01:04:41.539 --> 01:04:42.380 <v PXA> The Australians.
01:04:42.380 --> 01:04:44.179 <v Edward Miller> The Australians were using––
01:04:44.179 --> 01:04:45.340 <v PXA> Working for the Americans.
01:04:45.340 --> 01:04:47.219 <v Edward Miller> I see, were using the dairy farm to get intelligence.
01:04:47.219 --> 01:05:32.929 <v PXA> Yeah, so <c.529>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c>, he heard that in <c.530>Saigon</c> they have fresh milk. The <c.531>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c> people, to flatter him, they ask the people in <c.532>Saigon</c> to get him one or two cows, good ones, to send to Hue—when <c.533>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c>, he like dog, he like birds, he like everything. He like animal, like <c.534>Ngô Ðình Diệm</c> too, he like nature...and so then he like the German shepherd. And then <c.535><c.537>Phạm Quốc Thuần</c></c>, the Minister of Defense. After that he was deputy, he was minister at the palace, <c.536>Nguyễn Quốc Thuần</c>—Phạm Quốc Thuần.
01:05:32.929 --> 01:05:34.650 <v Edward Miller> <c.538>Phạm Quốc Thuần</c>.
01:05:34.650 --> 01:06:20.050 <v PXA> Yeah, and then order this man to get two German shepherds. So they have plenty of German shepherds bought by the Americans given to the Vietnamese army and trained at <c.539>Bến Cát</c>...trained at not very far from here, they call the place they train German shepherds for operation. They select good ones to send to <c.540><c.541>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c></c>, and Ngô Ðình Cẩn very happy. You know, the flatterer very dangerous, very dangerous are the flatterer; they wait until Mr. <c.542>Thuần</c>, you know, <c.543>Phạm Quốc Thuần</c>, returned to <c.544>Saigon</c> and they report to <c.545>Cẩn</c>.
01:06:20.050 --> 01:06:24.289 <v Edward Miller> And they brought the cows up to <c.546>Huế</c>?
01:06:24.289 --> 01:08:19.199 <v PXA> These people brought the cows already. This time, two German shepherds. And good ones, you what I mean? Well-trained and very– you can use it to attack or order him to do anything [phone rings]…This time two German shepherds, <c.547>Phạm Quốc Thuần</c>, you know. The minister brought two, because he minister, I think, of defense, and brought two dogs from the German shepherd training…So over there, and they didn’t say anything. He look at the dog and they very, very nice. And the flatterer does work for him say, “Alright take care of the dog,” so he took the dog, I’m going to talk to him for a while and Mr. <c.548><c.550>Thuần</c></c> returns to <c.549><c.551>Saigon</c></c>. They wait until Mr. Thuần returns to Saigon. They come and talk to <c.552>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c>. They say, “Ông cậu”—they call him “Ông”—“Minister look down upon you, he has no regard for you, he gave you the dog but he doesn't give the name. How can you call the dog in? While you’re chewing betel, how you call him? [makes clicking sound, calling a dog] You can call him that way? While chewing it, you have to spit out the betel and call in the dog. [clicking sound] And you call him that way he couldn't come. You see it? He is so hot, arrogant. He look at you, representative of <c.553>Central Vietnam</c>—nothing!” You see that, you see the sign of the Minister, he very mad about that. He told me that, you know?
01:08:19.199 --> 01:08:23.279 <v Edward Miller> The minister you’re talking about, you said, is this <c.554>Nguyễn Quốc Thuần</c>?
01:08:23.279 --> 01:08:29.439 <v PXA> No, <c.555>Phạm Quốc Thuần</c>, I think...or <c.556>Nguyễn Quốc Thuần</c>, something like that. You check the...
01:08:29.439 --> 01:08:31.840 <v Edward Miller> He was Minister of the Economy?
01:08:31.840 --> 01:08:34.439 <v PXA> No, Minister of Defense. He had replaced
01:08:34.439 --> 01:08:40.815 <v Edward Miller> <c.557>Trần Trung Dung</c>.
01:08:40.815 --> 01:08:48.880 <v PXA> He had replaced <c.558>Trần Trung Dung</c>, Nguyễn Quốc Thuần, I think, something like that, Nguyễn Quốc Thuần. After that he became minister of the presidency.
01:08:48.880 --> 01:08:54.000 <v Edward Miller> That’s right, and he spoke English very well, right? He was very close to many Americans.
01:08:54.000 --> 01:09:03.636 <v PXA> That’s right, that’s right. So he order his men to bring two dogs when he pay the visit to <c.559>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c>.
01:09:03.636 --> 01:09:08.000 <v Edward Miller> Right, but the flatterers, the Catholics undermine him.
01:09:08.000 --> 01:09:34.199 <v PXA> He make the mistake of not telling, giving the name of the two dogs, and how to call him. They use it against <c.560><c.561>Thuần</c></c> because they don’t like Thuần. They know that Thuần is very close to <c.562>Trần Trung Dung</c> and <c.563>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c> —uh, <c.564>Ngô Ðình Nhu</c>...not close to...So he select his own men, like the chief of Vietnamese press, <c.565>Nguyễn Thái</c> is his man.
01:09:34.199 --> 01:09:34.640 <v Edward Miller> Is whose man?
01:09:34.640 --> 01:09:35.600 <v PXA> <c.566>Nguyễn Thái</c>.
01:09:35.600 --> 01:09:37.501 <v Edward Miller> Yes, I know [of] <c.567>Nguyễn Thái</c>.
01:09:37.501 --> 01:09:40.159 <v PXA> He very nice, he's the man––
01:09:40.159 --> 01:09:44.079 <v EM> And he was a man of <c.568>Thuần</c>’s?
01:09:44.079 --> 01:09:46.840 <v PXA> Yeah, of <c.569>Cẩn</c>.
01:09:46.840 --> 01:09:48.279 <v EM> Of <c.570><c.571>Cẩn</c></c>, he was a man of Cẩn’s, really?
01:09:48.279 --> 01:09:49.880 <v PXA> From <c.572>Huế</c>.
01:09:49.880 --> 01:09:51.119 <v EM> He was from <c.573>Huế</c> as well?
01:09:51.119 --> 01:10:13.239 <v PXA> He was recruited by <c.574>Cẩn</c> people when the Americans decided to recruit the Vietnamese when they signed agreement with the French. They started recruiting Vietnamese who graduated from high school, the baccalaureate, to send to <c.575>U.S.</c> for training for five-, four-year university. About ten of them.
01:10:13.239 --> 01:10:14.520 <v EM> And <c.576>Nguyễn Thái</c> was one of them?
01:10:14.520 --> 01:10:46.760 <v PXA> Yes, but from <c.577>Central Vietnam</c> should be decided by <c.578>Ngô Ðình Cẩn</c>, you see that? He very smart. So he returned here, one of the first ten Vietnamese loyal to <c.579>Diệm</c> to return from the <c.580>U.S.</c> here, to serve the regime. And <c.581>Nguyễn Thái</c> one of them. You see his picture, very young, even though at that time, he about thirty-four, thirty-five years old.
01:10:46.760 --> 01:10:50.079 <v EM> So that’s <c.582>Nguyễn Thái</c>, and––
01:10:50.079 --> 01:11:00.600 <v PXA> I don’t know this one, this is the Filipino colonel, full <c.583>Colonel Benson</c>.
01:11:00.600 --> 01:11:01.800 <v EM> Valeriano?
01:11:01.800 --> 01:11:05.000 <v PXA> No, friend of Valeriano, <c.584>Colonel Benson</c>.
01:11:05.000 --> 01:11:06.600 <v EM> Benson?<c.585></c>
01:11:06.600 --> 01:11:20.789 <v PXA> Yeah. This is Lieutenant Sharp of the Navy. They graduated from the <c.586>Fort Bragg</c>, psychological warfare. They came to <c.587>Vietnam</c> to work together.<c.588></c>
01:11:20.789 --> 01:11:22.670 <v EM> That's <c.589>Nguyễn Thái</c>.
01:11:22.670 --> 01:11:24.270 <v PXA> I forgot the guy. This guy.
01:11:24.270 --> 01:11:55.149 <v EM> Okay. I'm sure––I think we should probably finish up here because I know you've not been feeling well. Let me ask you one more question, though, about the Buddhist movement in <c.590>1963</c>, Phong trào Phật giáo. And of course, that begins in <c.591><c.592>Huế</c></c>. My question is, why does it begin in Huế? And is it a movement that's a reaction against <c.593>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> or against <c.594>Ngô Đình Thục</c>?
01:11:55.149 --> 01:12:08.949 <v PXA> It's against <c.595><c.596>Ngô Đình Thục</c></c>, because Ngô Đình Thục would like to convert the people into Catholic in order to have the big number to be made cardinal. You cannot be made cardinal with a small number of Catholic power.
01:12:08.949 --> 01:12:11.949 <v EM> Right. So he needs he needs a lot of conversions.
01:12:11.949 --> 01:12:47.000 <v PXA> That's right, that's right. That's the reason. And <c.597>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> forced them. That's why in <c.598>Vietnam</c> we have three kinds of Catholic: lay down Catholic, born Catholic. And the knee down Catholic, I mean flatterer who followed the regime by converting themselves into Catholic. The standing up Catholic laymen, those who married Catholic to become Catholic. There are three kinds of Catholics in <c.599>Vietnam</c>: Born Catholic, knee down Catholic, and then standing up Catholic.
01:12:47.000 --> 01:13:03.270 <v EM> Standing up––for if you marry? So do you think that at that time, if <c.600>Ngô Đình Thục</c> had not been made Archbishop of <c.601>Huế</c>, there would be no Buddhist movement because the relations between–
01:13:03.270 --> 01:16:47.970 <v PXA> The Buddhist movement is t<c.602>his, it belongs</c> to the international Buddhist movement. They called it in the early 30s or something like that. The Buddhists know that if they don't get together, they can never be strong, like the Muslim or the Catholic. That's why they get together in <c.603>Ceylon</c>, to set up the unification of Buddhists, all the sects. That's what they call it Viet... The same for the Vietnamese, they call it <c.604>Phật giáo Việt Nam Thống Nhất</c> because of that one. The first unified one. And in <c.605>Ceylon</c> and <c.606>Vietnam</c>, they send there Mr.–he's now running the the Buddhist school here––high school––and confiscated by the government. He went there. He was born <c.607>1919</c>, <c.608>'18</c> or <c.609>'19</c>? So he went to that conference in over 30. And then the second one we had, in <c.610>Japan</c>. Third one was in <c.611>Phnom Penh</c> or something like that. So the Americans know the Buddhist, the majority of Vietnamese follow the Buddhist . They are not Buddhists, but they more or less follow, influenced by the Buddhist. And then––that's not <c.612>Ngô Đình Diệm</c>––he influenced it. [inaudible] So they have to build constituents by forcing that. It won't work. So the Americans know about that. So they have to work with the Buddhists in case things happen. And they will be ready. And they use <c.613>Trí Quang</c>. <c.617>Trí Quang</c> is very important. He's from <c.614>Quảng Bình</c>. He's from <c.615><c.619>Võ Nguyên Giáp</c></c> village. <c.616><c.618>Đỗ Mậu</c></c> was also from this village. So they all three came from the same village. <c.620>Trí Quang</c>, Đỗ Mậu, and Võ Nguyên Giáp, and many others. When the Việt Minh came to power, the family of <c.621>Trí Quang</c> give support to them. But because of the extremists. They call it three no's, if you follow the communist regime, you have three no's: No family, no religion, no country. You have three no's. You work for the world and the International. So three no's. That's why they burn one of the monks, such as the uncle of <c.622>Trí Quang</c> alive. For some reason, because that one had some land, et cetera. And the local people, the peasant class, followers of communists, et cetera, and it's stupid. Not highly political, highly educated. They killed the man by burning. That image impressed into the head of Trí Quang. That's why <c.623>Thích Quảng Đức</c> burn. Because of that.
01:16:47.970 --> 01:16:49.369 <v EM> <c.624>Thích Quảng Đức</c> burns?
01:16:49.369 --> 01:16:54.369 <v PXA> Because of that image, he urged <c.625>Thích Quảng Đức</c> to burn.
01:16:54.369 --> 01:16:56.289 <v EM> <c.626>Trí Quang</c> urged <c.627>Thích Quảng Đức</c> to burn himself?
01:16:56.289 --> 01:17:46.010 <v PXA> Yeah. That's his idea. And after that, many other monks burned themselves because of that image. And then he started working for <c.628>French G2</c> against the <c.629>Việt Minh</c>. The French had all the documents brought into <c.630>Saigon</c> after the <c.631>Geneva Agreement</c> was signed, and <c.632>Trí Quang</c> went to <c.633>Huế</c> to carry his activity at the <c.634>Từ Đàm pagoda</c>. And <c.635>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> people know about that. My cousin knows about that. So with the American advisors, they have to treat them very well. In the future, they know that if you make them mad, they will against the regime––they will be against the regime. So the Americans used the Buddhists as a reserve card. I see.
01:17:46.010 --> 01:17:50.210 <v EM> But at first, the relationship between <c.636>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> and the Buddhists was good?
01:17:50.210 --> 01:17:54.329 <v PXA> Always good, always good.
01:17:54.329 --> 01:17:56.529 <v EM> But why did it go bad?
01:17:56.529 --> 01:17:58.000 <v PXA> Go bad because––
01:17:58.000 --> 01:17:59.000 <v EM> Because of <c.637>Thục</c>?
01:17:59.000 --> 01:18:16.960 <v PXA> Because of <c.638><c.639>Thục</c></c>. When the other people––because Thục did not want––You know, in <c.640>Huế</c> family, traditional family, the young people should take the order of the elders. Not only that, but he's also the bishop––archbishop, not bishop.
01:18:16.960 --> 01:18:18.119 <v EM> He has a lot of authority.
01:18:18.119 --> 01:18:40.479 <v PXA> Yes, authority. So <c.641>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> agreed to follow to forbid the flags. And the people were very mad about that, so they demonstrated. And then <c.642>Ngô Đình Thục</c> ordered his men to throw the grenade.
01:18:40.479 --> 01:18:41.479 <v EM> To throw the grenade?
01:18:41.479 --> 01:18:45.039 <v PXA> Yeah. Many killed. That's very bad.
01:18:45.039 --> 01:19:17.279 <v EM> Because I read the the Hồi ký of <c.643>Trí Quang</c> in <c.644>1964</c> or <c.645>'65</c>. He published in Tạp chí Hải Triều Âm. He said that on that day, on May 8th, 1963, he met with <c.646><c.647>Cẩn</c></c> before the incident. Cẩn said that he would call <c.648>Saigon</c> and he would rescind the order. But of course, that didn't happen, so I'm wondering if <c.649>Thục</c> overruled?
01:19:17.279 --> 01:19:21.439 <v PXA> <c.650>Thục</c> overruled. Because my cousin told me <c.651>Thục</c> overruled it.
01:19:21.439 --> 01:19:23.760 <v EM> And your cousin again is––
01:19:23.760 --> 01:19:27.960 <v PXA> Chief of Police and Security of <c.652>Central Vietnam</c>.
01:19:27.960 --> 01:19:29.560 <v EM> Lê Khắc Duyệt?<c.653></c>
01:19:29.560 --> 01:19:31.159 <v PXA> Duyệt. D-U-Y-E-T.
01:19:31.159 --> 01:19:35.560 <v EM> Right, okay. And he was still the chief of security at that time?
01:19:35.560 --> 01:19:36.239 <v PXA> He was.
01:19:36.239 --> 01:19:37.800 <v EM> And he was a Buddhist?
01:19:37.800 --> 01:19:42.000 <v PXA> He Buddhist. Buddhist follower. He vegetarian too.
01:19:42.000 --> 01:19:48.720 <v EM> He told you that afterwards? He told you that <c.654>Cẩn</c> had been overruled?
01:19:48.720 --> 01:20:43.119 <v PXA> So the point in this is <c.655>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> very smart. If <c.656>Ngô Đình Nhu</c> or <c.657>Diệm</c> listened to him, maybe the regime would last longer. Maybe, I'm not sure. Very difficult to tell for the mandarins, they can make a mistake by using them as the leader of the country. But after that, they keep to the Buddhists. The Buddhists don't know about politics. The Catholics know politics, but the Buddhists don't know it. So they need the Americans to teach them. So to clear all the file of <c.658>Trí Quang</c> working for <c.659>French G2</c>, the Americans ordered the Vietnamese to do it. But please don't publish this: Dr. <c.660>Tuyến</c>, he was asked by the chief of <c.661>CIA</c>, I think <c.662>de Silva</c>.
01:20:43.119 --> 01:20:44.239 <v EM> Who?
01:20:44.239 --> 01:20:49.359 <v PXA> <c.663>de Silva</c>. He's the chief <c.664>CIA</c> here.
01:20:49.359 --> 01:20:50.560 <v EM> <c.665>Colby</c>?
01:20:50.560 --> 01:20:51.960 <v PXA> <c.666>No. Before Co</c>lby.
01:20:51.960 --> 01:20:52.239 <v EM> Before <c.667>Colby</c>?
01:20:52.239 --> 01:20:54.319 <v PXA> <c.668>de Silva</c>.
01:20:54.319 --> 01:20:55.439 <v EM> <c.669>de Silva</c>?
01:20:55.439 --> 01:21:01.590 <v PXA> Yeah. To take all the files and burn it.
01:21:01.590 --> 01:21:02.710 <v EM> Which files?
01:21:02.710 --> 01:21:23.390 <v PXA> The files left by the <c.670>French G2</c> and the police, about <c.671>Trí Quang</c> and burn it, so no trace. Then he was sent to <c.672>Cambodia</c> as a representative of Buddhist at the meeting of the Buddhist unification.
01:21:23.390 --> 01:21:26.989 <v EM> <c.673>Trí Quang</c> would be sent?
01:21:26.989 --> 01:21:45.710 <v PXA> So <c.674>Tuyến</c> had a lot of enemies, he told me about that. But anyway, it's a secret. Even though he died, I don't want to know about that. Not to divulge this one, unless they agree to declassify, but I don't think the Americans would declassify.
01:21:45.710 --> 01:21:46.590 <v EM> Not yet.
01:21:46.590 --> 01:21:48.550 <v PXA> No, I don't think they would do it.
01:21:48.550 --> 01:21:50.069 <v EM> Right.
01:21:50.069 --> 01:21:58.989 <v PXA> But that's why some people want me to write a memo. I never––I don't want to do it, but this is for your knowledge.
01:21:58.989 --> 01:22:03.750 <v EM> I appreciate that very much because this is this is very useful to me because it helps me––
01:22:03.750 --> 01:22:27.750 <v PXA> The reason is I know the Buddhist will create hell, thanks to a <c.675>CIA</c> who was a professor in <c.676>Huế</c>. I'll tell you the name too– Mr. <c.677>Jerry Rose</c>. He worked for the <c.678>Evening Star</c> and <c.679>the Washington Post</c>, et cetera. He's a good friend of <c.680><c.681>Stanley</c> Karnow</c>. Stanley, and he's my good friend too.
01:22:27.750 --> 01:22:28.510 <v EM> And he was <c.682>CIA</c>?
01:22:28.510 --> 01:23:26.000 <v PXA> He was––actually professor of English or something like that. He graduated from <c.683>Sorbonne</c>. He taught in <c.684>Huế</c>. He speaks Vietnamese a little bit, but not much. So because of the problem with adultery, particularly Mr. <c.685>Barnes</c> with the council in <c.686>Huế</c>, but his wife was involved with <c.687>Jerry Rose</c>. The man has a cold, you know––Mr. Barnes, the council, he had a cold blood. He found that, you know, flagrante deli[cto], but instead of pulling out a pistol and kill, he didn't do it. But he said, all right, you better go. And he left, he dared not stay in <c.688>Huế</c>, so he quit and he ran to <c.689>Saigon</c>.
01:23:26.000 --> 01:23:27.859 <v EM> So then he came to <c.690>Saigon</c>.
01:23:27.859 --> 01:23:53.899 <v PXA> He told me when he worked for a jou<c.691>rnalist at the Wash</c>ington Post or Evening Post––<c.692>Evening Star</c>, something like that. He told me, Ẩn, you know a lot of people in <c.693>Huế</c>, you have to watch the Buddhists in the future, and you may have a scoop for <c.694>Reuters</c>. I did not know that was important, he told me about that in <c.695>1962</c>.
01:23:53.899 --> 01:23:58.300 <v EM> So the <c.696>CIA</c> was already concerned about the Buddhists in <c.697>Huế</c>?
01:23:58.300 --> 01:24:06.420 <v PXA> They know about that! They know about that. They organize this kind of thing. Even they<c.698> organize</c>d Trí Quang to go to the embassy too.
01:24:06.420 --> 01:24:08.000 <v EM> In <c.699>'63</c>?
01:24:08.000 --> 01:24:41.939 <v PXA> <c.700>'63</c>, yeah, when they revolted. [inaudible] follow the situation there, the Buddhists. [inaudible] All right, so I asked Mr. [inaudible] and my people over there to watch very closely for any sign unusual. Just call me from <c.701>Huế</c>. And maybe they call in <c.702>1963</c> about that, about <c.703>Ngô Đình Thục</c>, et cetera.
01:24:41.939 --> 01:24:43.779 <v EM> Before May, the signs were already there?
01:24:43.779 --> 01:25:31.979 <v PXA> And actually, I [inaudible], so I got the scoop for <c.704>Reuters</c> too. So <c.705>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> is very smart, even at the courtroom. When <c.706>Nguyễn Khánh</c> sent him to the court, he was sentenced to death. He was sentenced to death at the military court, he and <c.707>Dương Văn Hiếu</c>––the one who worked for him and kidnapped all the communists and pro-communists in the south in <c.708>Saigon</c> here. They were sent to the military court because of illegal action; both of them carry [out] illegal action against civilians.
01:25:31.979 --> 01:25:34.060 <v EM> So when did this take place?
01:25:34.060 --> 01:25:40.340 <v PXA> In <c.709>1960</c>. <c.710>1965</c>––<c.711>'64</c>.
01:25:40.340 --> 01:25:43.500 <v EM> <c.712>'64</c>. This is when <c.713>Cẩn</c> has been captured?
01:25:43.500 --> 01:26:02.151 <v PXA> But that's after the coup. [inaudible] And <c.714>Nguyễn Khánh</c> overthrow the first junta, and then he sent them to the military court. The head of the military court, the judge, was <c.715>Dương Hiếu Nghĩa</c>, and the other one is <c.716>Nguyễn Hoà Hiệp</c>.
01:26:02.151 --> 01:26:09.000 <v EM> Nguyễn Hiếu Nghĩa? Was he––
01:26:09.000 --> 01:27:12.210 <v PXA> Colonel <c.717>Dương Hiếu Nghĩa</c>. He was Province Chief later in <c.718>Vĩnh Long</c>, et cetera. He's the <c.719>Đại Việt</c> leader. And <c.720>Nguyễn Hoà Hiệp</c>, the [Vietnamese?], he is Minister of Information. So, both of them sit there as the judge, with another one I forgot, but these two men were. So, they questioned him, and <c.721>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> answered very well, very politely, fluently. One was "Thưa quý toà, tôi chỉ có là Cố vấn Phong trào Cách mạng Quốc gia thôi, tôi không có quyền gì hết. Nói là tôi bắt người này kia là không đúng." He was very smart, he denied everything, but the other one cannot. The other one asked for one thing: We capture one very important general, a <c.722>VC</c> general. You can sentence me to lie in prison, alright, but release me for a while so I can recapture that man, and then I will go back to jail.
01:27:12.210 --> 01:27:12.689 <v EM> <c.723>Cẩn</c> said this?
01:27:12.689 --> 01:27:58.560 <v PXA> No. <c.724>Dương Văn Hiếu</c>, the Chief of <c.725>Secret Police</c> in <c.726><c.729>Central Vietnam</c></c>. Actually, they decided lif<c.728>e imprisonmen</c>t for <c.727>Dương Văn Hiếu</c>–Chief of Secret Police in Central Vietnam. And <c.730>Ngô Đình Cẩn</c> sentenced to death. You know the reason why he was sentenced to death? He refused to return $2 million or $3 million in the bank in <c.731>Switzerland</c> to General <c.732>Khánh</c>. Instead, he gave it to the <c.733>Catholic Church</c>. That's why he deserved to be killed.
01:27:58.560 --> 01:28:04.760 <v EM> I see. So, if he had given the money then, <c.734>Khánh</c> would not have executed him?
01:28:04.760 --> 01:28:13.319 <v PXA> That's right. He would have been released. <c.735>Trần Văn Đôn</c> know about that.
01:28:13.319 --> 01:28:14.840 <v EM> <c.736>Trần Văn Đôn</c>? Oh! The general.
01:28:14.840 --> 01:28:50.840 <v PXA> Yeah, the one who pulled the coup. The one who planned the coup was <c.737>Lê Văn Kim</c>, his brother in law. To execute the coup, <c.738>Trần Văn Đôn</c>. Both of them are very good friends of [inaudible name] and <c.739>Lou Conein</c>. That's why these guys get together all the time. So I was there very often with them too. That's the reason why I know. But please write very carefully about that.
